text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocker(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
InClass(x) ::: x is in a class.
Michael(x) ::: x is Michael.
Jump(x) ::: x jumps.
Shooting(x) ::: x is shooting.
Windy(x) ::: x is Windy.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y) → Blocker(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
Man(michael) ∧ ∀x (InClass(x) ∧ x ≠ michael → Taller(michael, x)) ::: Michael is a man who is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z (Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If person x is taller than person y, and person y is taller than person z, then x is taller than z.
Man(peter) ∧ Taller(peter, michael) ::: Peter is a man who is taller than Michael.
∀x (Man(michael) ∧ Blocker(michael, x) → ¬Jump(x)) ::: Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting.
¬Blocker(michael, windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Shooting(x) ∧ Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.

Conclusion:
Blocker(peter, windy) ::: Peter can block Windy's shooting.
